title: Hidden orchard
notes: Keep one adult at each table; an adult may hold the origin while the child chooses targets. On return, K-1 can compare blocker counts (P3), rows (P4), or which visible dots hide the most (P5). Grades 2-3 can group dots by direction (P4), then use the number-rule and visible-row questions (P5-6). Grades 4-5 can predict far targets (P3), complete ray groups (P4), explain both directions of the criterion (P5), or justify exact blocker counts (P6-7). Saved sight lines should pass through dot centers; thread thickness is not a mathematical blocker. On the 7 mm grid of Grades 4-5 P3 the thread cannot settle (13,8): it passes 0.46 mm from the centers of (5,3) and (8,5), and there the rule beats the thread.
